nodes.name: Stamp & Shape Email
nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes messageId, receivedAt. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

nodes.name: Payload Valid?
nodes.notes: Two-way gate on ={{ $json.messageId }}. TRUE continues the happy path, FALSE takes the alternate branch. Watch out: The false branch carries the non-matching items — wire it deliberately rather than leaving it dangling.

nodes.name: Record Rejected Input
nodes.notes: Creates a new record in Airtable's 'Emails' table. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. Credential: Airtable PAT. airtable.com/create/tokens → create a Personal Access Token.

nodes.name: Score the Lead
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Score each email 0-100 from simple heuristics Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Assign Round-Robin Owner
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Round-robin owner assignment Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Route by Heat
nodes.notes: Routes each item to one of 3 lanes: hot, warm + fallback. Watch out: Unmatched items go to the fallback output; without one they are silently dropped.

nodes.name: Hot → Google Sheets + Instant Ping
nodes.notes: Upserts a row into 'Email Tracker', matched on messageId — re-running with the same key updates the row instead of duplicating it. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2 / service account. Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.

nodes.name: Notify Assigned Owner
nodes.notes: Posts a message to Slack — a low-latency way for the team to see automation activity without checking a dashboard. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Slack OAuth2. Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.

nodes.name: Warm → Drip via Gmail
nodes.notes: Sends an email via Gmail — subject is the first line of the message body, recipient comes from the item's email field. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Google OAuth2. Google Cloud Console → enable Gmail API → OAuth consent screen → OAuth client ID (Web).

nodes.name: Cold → Park in Nurture List
nodes.notes: Creates a new record in Airtable's 'table' table. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. On failure the item leaves via the error output instead of stopping the run. Credential: Airtable PAT. airtable.com/create/tokens → create a Personal Access Token.

nodes.name: Combine Lead Paths
nodes.notes: Rejoins 3 branches into one stream (mode: append) so downstream logic runs once. Watch out: Waits for every configured input. If one branch never produces items, add 'Always Output Data' upstream so this doesn't stall.

nodes.name: Fingerprint for Idempotency
nodes.notes: Custom JavaScript: Build a stable idempotency key per email (djb2 hash, no deps) Watch out: Must return an array of items shaped like [{ json: {...} }].

nodes.name: Drop Already-Processed Items
nodes.notes: Cross-execution dedupe: remembers keys it has processed before and drops repeats — the idempotency guard. Watch out: Cross-execution memory persists. After changing the key field, clear stored keys or old keys keep matching.

nodes.name: Stamp Completion Time
nodes.notes: Stamps completedAt with the current time for auditing.

nodes.name: Persist Run Metadata
nodes.notes: Saves key fields onto the execution record — searchable later in n8n's execution list.

nodes.name: Summarize Run Stats
nodes.notes: Shapes the item: writes runAt, itemCount, status. Keeps the schema explicit between stages.

nodes.notes: Appends a new row to 'Email Tracker' — a human-readable audit trail that doesn't require opening n8n to inspect. Retries 3x with 2s backoff before giving up. # Capture applications: Slack for newsletters

**Pattern:** Form Intake · **Level:** Advanced · **Trigger:** Form

## Overview

Starts when the form is submitted, and covers newsletters work end to end across Slack, Airtable, Google Sheets and Gmail.

It moves through 19 working steps plus a 3-node error rail, in this order:

1. New Email Form Submission
2. Stamp & Shape Email
3. Payload Valid?
4. Record Rejected Input
5. Score the Lead
6. Assign Round-Robin Owner
7. Route by Heat
8. Hot → Google Sheets + Instant Ping
9. Notify Assigned Owner
10. Warm → Drip via Gmail
11. Cold → Park in Nurture List
12. Combine Lead Paths
13. Fingerprint for Idempotency
14. Drop Already-Processed Items
15. Stamp Completion Time
16. Persist Run Metadata
17. Summarize Run Stats
18. Append Audit Row (Google Sheets)
19. Send Summary to Slack

Anything that throws leaves the happy path at that node and goes down the red rail — Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack → Park in Dead-Letter Queue — so a failure is reported rather than silently lost.

## Why it exists

Doing newsletters work by hand is slow and easy to get wrong, and it stops entirely when the person who does it is away. This makes the process repeatable and monitored, with failures surfaced instead of silently lost.

## Main flow

New Email Form Submission → Stamp & Shape Email → Payload Valid? → Record Rejected Input → Score the Lead → Assign Round-Robin Owner → Route by Heat → Hot → Google Sheets + Instant Ping → Notify Assigned Owner → Warm → Drip via Gmail → Cold → Park in Nurture List → Combine Lead Paths → Fingerprint for Idempotency → Drop Already-Processed Items → Stamp Completion Time → Persist Run Metadata → Summarize Run Stats → Append Audit Row (Google Sheets) → Send Summary to Slack → Capture Failure Context → Escalate Failure to Slack → Park in Dead-Letter Queue

## Use it for

- Teams keeping Slack and Airtable aligned by hand for newsletters
- Intake checked for completeness before it is stored in Slack, for newsletters
- Newsletters work where "Stamp & Shape Email" is still a manual step before Slack
- Newsletters work that only reaches Slack when a form is submitted, when someone remembers to start it

## You get

- Keeps Slack and Airtable in step for newsletters, without anyone re-typing a row
- Safe to re-run: records already in Slack or Airtable are skipped, across all 22 nodes of this newsletters build
- A failed Slack or Airtable call is retried rather than dropped, at any of the 22 nodes in this newsletters build
- Branches rejoin before Slack, so a newsletters run reports once rather than 22 times
- Every newsletters run leaves an audit row behind, alongside Slack

## Before first run
Connect credentials: Airtable PAT; Google OAuth2; Google OAuth2 / service account; Slack OAuth2.
Follow the color key: 🟦 entry · 🟪 AI · 🟫 actions · ⬜ utilities · 🟩 outputs · 🟥 error rail.
Each node has its own doc card underneath — read those before editing.

## Try it now
Sample data is pinned on the trigger — hit **Execute Workflow** to watch it flow through every node before connecting any real credentials. Unpin the trigger (right-click → Unpin) when you're ready to go live.

## Design decisions

Round-robin owner assignment happens right after scoring, before routing — every lead gets an accountable owner regardless of tier, so even a 'cold' lead parked in the nurture list is someone's responsibility later, not an anonymous row in a spreadsheet.

## Practice exercises

Already production-grade — deepen your understanding:

1. Change the hot/warm threshold values and watch the tier distribution shift.
2. Add a 4th owner to the round-robin pool.
3. Add a follow-up wait+check to the warm-drip branch, similar to the drip-ladder spine.

## Credentials setup

Credentials are never included in a template file, so every node below needs its own connection before the first real run. In n8n: open the node, click the Credential dropdown, choose **Create new**.

**Airtable PAT**
airtable.com/create/tokens → create a Personal Access Token.
_Gotcha:_ Scope the token to the specific base, and grant `data.records:write`. Field names are case-sensitive.

**Google OAuth2 / service account**
Google Cloud Console → enable Sheets API → OAuth2 client, or a Service Account.
_Gotcha:_ Using a Service Account? Share the spreadsheet with its email address or it 404s.

**Slack OAuth2**
Slack API → Your Apps → create an app → OAuth & Permissions. n8n's Slack OAuth2 credential walks the install for you.
_Gotcha:_ Needs `chat:write`. Invite the bot to the channel or posting fails with `not_in_channel`.

**Google OAuth2**
Google Cloud Console → enable Gmail API → OAuth consent screen → OAuth client ID (Web).
_Gotcha:_ Add n8n's OAuth redirect URL exactly as shown in the credential, or the consent loop fails.

Set each credential up once and it is reusable across every workflow in your instance.

## Troubleshooting

**Workflow does nothing when the trigger should fire**
Cause: It is still a draft, or the trigger is inactive.
Fix: Publish/activate the workflow. Manual test runs use a different URL than production.

**A node shows a red error triangle on import**
Cause: No credential is attached yet.
Fix: Expected on a fresh import — open the node and attach a credential (see the Credentials setup note).

**Execution stalls at the Merge node**
Cause: One input branch produced no items, so Merge is still waiting.
Fix: Enable 'Always Output Data' on the node feeding the empty branch.

Still stuck? n8n's **Executions** tab shows the exact node that failed and the data going into it — start there rather than guessing.

## 🛟 Error handling & retries

External calls retry **3× with 2s backoff**. Anything still failing exits through its node's error output into the red error rail → context is captured and the on-call channel is alerted. Failures are also parked in a dead-letter queue for replay. Set an n8n **Error Workflow** in settings as the final safety net.

## 🧹 Data quality

Dedupe/diff steps make re-runs safe: the same input twice will not create duplicate records. If you change the key fields, clear n8n's dedupe memory (node → 'Clear stored keys') before the next run.

## 🛠 Customize me

Quick wins: point the data nodes at your own accounts (see 🔑 lines on each card), adjust the trigger cadence, and tune thresholds/labels to your newsletters process. Every node card explains its role — safe to extend at any marked branch.

## 🔐 Security

Credentials live in n8n's credential store and are never written into node parameters — that is why this file carries none.

**Least privilege for this build**
- Slack: `chat:write` is enough to post. Do not add `channels:history` unless a node here actually reads messages.
- Airtable: scope the PAT to this one base and to `data.records:write`; a token scoped to the workspace can rewrite every base.
- Google Sheets: share the single spreadsheet with the service account rather than granting drive-wide access.
- Gmail: request the narrowest send/read scope the nodes need — full mailbox access is rarely required.

**Do not log**
newsletters payloads carry personal data (names, email addresses, phone numbers). Log the record id and the outcome, not the record. n8n retains full execution data by default — turn that down for this workflow in Settings → Executions if these runs touch real contacts.
